title: Testing Node code
summary: The built-in test runner, test doubles, testing async code and timers, and integration tests for HTTP handlers.

sections.title: node:test
sections.body:
Node ships a test runner: `import { test, describe } from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, run with `node --test`. It supports subtests, hooks (`before`, `afterEach`), mocking, coverage and watch mode. Vitest and Jest offer the same ideas with more conveniences.

Prefer `assert.deepStrictEqual` for structures and `await assert.rejects(promise, /message/)` for async failures.

sections.title: Test doubles
sections.body:
A **stub** returns canned answers, a **spy** records calls, a **mock** combines both with expectations, and a **fake** is a light working implementation such as an in-memory repository. Inject dependencies (pass the clock, the HTTP client or the repository in) so tests can swap them without patching modules.

Fake timers (`mock.timers.enable()` in `node:test`, `vi.useFakeTimers()` in Vitest) let you test retries and timeouts without waiting.

sections.title: Testing HTTP
sections.body: For handlers, start the app on port 0 (a random free port) in a `before` hook and use `fetch`, or use a helper like supertest that calls the app without a real port. Test the contract: status codes, headers and body shape, including error paths. Use a real database in a container for integration tests and reset it between tests.

pitfalls: Forgetting to `await` an async assertion, so the test passes before it runs.
Tests that depend on each other or on execution order.
Real timers and sleeps that make the suite slow and flaky.
Mocking so much that the test only checks the mocks.

gotchas.question: Why can `assert.rejects(fn())` without `await` pass when it should fail?
gotchas.answer: `assert.rejects` returns a promise. If the test does not await it, the test function finishes first and reports success; the failure surfaces later or not at all. Always `await` it.

gotchas.question: How do you test code that calls `Date.now()`?
gotchas.answer: Inject a clock (`now: () => number`) and pass a fake in tests, or use the test runner's fake timers and set the system time. Avoid tests that compare against the real current time.

gotchas.question: Unit, integration or end-to-end?
gotchas.answer: Unit tests cover pure logic quickly; integration tests check that your code works with real infrastructure such as a database; end-to-end tests drive the whole system the way a user does. A healthy suite has many unit tests, a solid set of integration tests and a few end-to-end tests.
